recognize_zh: 一顆大型巨噬／單核細胞具豐富空泡狀細胞質，其內與邊緣有數顆褐黑色瘧色素（hemozoin）顆粒；旁邊帶狀與分葉中性球也含褐色顆粒，周圍紅血球內可見細小環狀體，符合惡性瘧原蟲感染的含色素吞噬細胞。
features: Large macrophage/monocyte with abundant finely vacuolated pale cytoplasm and an oval nucleus
Several discrete brown-black hemozoin pigment granules within and at the edge of the macrophage cytoplasm
Adjacent band and segmented neutrophils containing small brown pigment granules
Many surrounding erythrocytes contain small ring forms, some with double chromatin dots
Faint area at the lower-left edge with smudged nuclear material
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a large macrophage with abundant vacuolated cytoplasm containing several discrete brown-black hemozoin pigment granules, adjacent to band and segmented neutrophils that also contain brown pigment. The surrounding erythrocytes are of normal size and many contain small, delicate ring forms, some with double chromatin dots. No schizonts are seen. Findings are consistent with Plasmodium falciparum malaria with pigment-laden phagocytes (macrophage and neutrophils).

ddx.vs: Hemosiderin is golden-yellow, coarse and Prussian blue positive, whereas hemozoin is brown-black, Prussian blue negative and accompanies intraerythrocytic parasites.
Melanin is fine brown granules in tumor cells or histiocytes without a background of ring-form parasitemia.
Precipitate is dark purple-black and lies on the slide surface across cells, not refractile brown granules within phagocytes.
Vivax also produces pigment-laden phagocytes but shows enlarged red cells with Schüffner dots and ameboid trophozoites.
